title: The Federal Reserve and Central Banking
text: The Federal Reserve System (the Fed) is the central banking system of the United States, established by the Federal Reserve Act in 1913. It has a dual mandate: to maximize employment and maintain stable prices (targeting 2% inflation). The Fed conducts monetary policy primarily through setting the federal funds rate — the interest rate at which banks lend to each other overnight — and through open market operations (buying and selling government securities). The Fed's main tools include interest rate setting, reserve requirements, and, since the 2008 financial crisis, quantitative easing (large-scale asset purchases). The Fed also acts as lender of last resort during financial crises.
